label.description: The region's accessible name, so a reader who lands in it is told what it is rather than hearing a message with no provenance. It names the STACK and never a toast: the messages inside it change, and a region renamed on every arrival is a region announced on every arrival.

live.description: polite, assertive or off: how the stack is announced. polite waits for a pause and is right for an outcome; assertive interrupts and is for the rare message that cannot wait. off is for a host that already says these things somewhere else — Jx Studio announces through its own single announcer, and a region here as well would say every notification twice. Role and attribute move together: polite writes role=status, assertive writes role=alert, off writes neither, so an assistive technology reading the role and one reading the attribute agree.

placement.description: bottom-end, bottom-start, top-end or top-start: which corner the stack is pinned to. It moves the box and NOT the order — the toasts are drawn in the order they are written, whichever corner they are in, so the order a reader hears, the order they tab through and the order they see stay one order. A host that wants the stack in the flow of its own layout overrides position in its own stylesheet; nothing here depends on the fixed box.

hotkey.description: The key that moves focus to the first control in the stack. It is what makes a recovery control reachable at all: the stack is at the end of the document and a toast may expire before a reader could Tab to it, so the reader asks for it in one press instead — and arriving suspends every clock in the stack, so nothing then expires under their hand. Escape gives focus back to where it came from, and so does a toast closing while the reader is in it. A press carrying Ctrl, Alt or Meta is left alone. Empty turns the gesture off, for an application that owns a command of its own for this.

onMount.description: Registers the stack's key on the document. It has to be the document: a key that only worked once focus was already in the stack would answer the question it exists to answer with itself.

onUnmount.description: Takes the key back when the stack leaves the document, so a removed host cannot go on answering a press for a stack it can no longer show.

onHold.description: Pointer or focus arrived anywhere in the stack: every toast in it is told to suspend its clock, not only the one underneath. An older toast retiring while the reader answers a newer one would move the very control they were reaching for.

onRelease.description: The pointer or the focus left the stack for something outside it, so the clocks run again. A move between two toasts of one stack is not a departure and releases nothing.

onClose.description: A toast closed. If it took the reader's focus with it, focus goes back to where the hotkey found it; if the reader was somewhere else entirely, nothing moves.

style.$description: aria-atomic is false and written out rather than left to the role, which supplies true: a stack re-read whole on every arrival would announce three old messages to deliver one new one. pointer-events is none on the box and auto on each toast, so the empty corner the stack reserves is not a hole the page cannot be clicked through.
